name: 112. OAuth2 Client-Controlled Field Lengths (RFC 6749 state/scope, RFC 7591 client_name/scope)
description: Regression for a customer report: GET /oauth2/authorize rejected any state parameter longer than 512 characters with error=server_error ("failed to create authorization request"), because oauth2_authorize_requests.state was varchar(512). Postgres enforces that bound (SQLite does not), so a Gemini Enterprise connector sending a 620-char base64 JSON state could never complete per-user authorisation. The same class applied to every other client-controlled column on the OAuth2 AS tables: oauth2_clients.client_name and .scope (RFC 7591 section 2 bounds neither) and the scope columns on oauth2_authorize_requests and oauth2_refresh_tokens (RFC 6749 section 3.3), all varchar(255). All five are now text; the request header block (server.read_buffer_size) is the effective limit. Case 1 registers a public client via DCR with a 1024-char client_name and a 200-token scope, asserts both are echoed, and chains its client_id. Case 2 sends a 620-char state (the reported size) with scope omitted, so the long registered scope is what gets stored. Case 3 sends a 4096-char state plus the full long scope explicitly. Both pin that the authorize step reaches consent (302 to /oauth/consent?flow=) with no error= in the redirect; redirect following is disabled on those items so the 302 itself is asserted. No provider spend. Note: against the default SQLite-backed harness profile these cases are green both before and after the fix; the bounds only ever fired on Postgres. They pin the contract for Postgres-backed profiles and against any future explicit length validation on these fields.
